71	a **changed normalized body** → keeps only **auto-fuzzable** ones (every param is scalar / String /
72	primitive array) → writes `manifest.json` + renamed `<Class>{Original,Refactored}.java` snapshots
73	into the **same package** (so both compile into one JVM).
74	
75	**Manifest `params` + `static` are read from the REFACTORED signature**
76	([build_project.py:87](scripts/build_project.py#L87), `classify(n[key]...)` where `n` = refactored).
77	Name+arity are shared by construction (pairing key = `name/paramCount`). Verified: **0 signature
78	disagreements** across all 62 apex-core methods, so original-vs-refactored is moot in practice.
79	**Conclusion: correct approach for signature-preserving refactorings.** If a refactoring *changes* a
80	param type → runtime `NoSuchMethodException` → **ERROR** (fail-safe); if it changes arity → the
81	methods don't pair → silently **dropped** (a known blind spot, never a false EQUIVALENT).
82	
83	**The fuzz loop** ([GenericDifferential.java](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java)):
84	Jazzer (libFuzzer-based, coverage-guided) drives a thin per-method harness →
85	`GenericDifferential.run(data, project, id)` → looks the spec up in the manifest → resolves **both**
86	`Original` and `Refactored` classes → builds the receiver (recursive ctor synthesis for instance
87	methods) and args **once** from the `FuzzedDataProvider` using the manifest `params` as the decode
88	schema → `copy()`s them per side → invokes each on a **3 s watchdog thread** → oracle compares. Jazzer
89	generates raw **byte inputs at runtime** (not test files); the only per-method *file* is the harness,
90	written by [gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) (Python). Corpus of "interesting" byte inputs
91	persists under `target/fuzz-cwd/.cifuzz-corpus/`.
92	
93	**The oracle** (`equivalent()`): DIVERGENT iff exception **types** differ, or (neither threw)
94	scalar/JDK **return values** differ. One-sided **TIMEOUT is inconclusive** (not divergent). Return
95	type used for comparability comes from the **original** method (`oM.getReturnType()`) — mirror image
96	of the params-from-refactored rule.

121	
122	| Dimension | Paper (Eq@DFuzz) | Our tool |
123	|---|---|---|
124	| Language | Python | Java |
125	| Fuzzer | Atheris (libFuzzer) | Jazzer (libFuzzer) — sibling |
126	| Unit tested | whole function / program | individual **changed method** (source-diffed) |
127	| Input typing | GPT-4-inferred + manually-validated constraints | heuristic scalar-only from signature |
128	| Complex-object args | handled via constraints | **excluded** at manifest time |
129	| Oracle | output equality only | return value **+ exception type**; TIMEOUT = inconclusive |
130	| Receiver/ctors | N/A (functional Python) | recursive ctor synthesis |
131	| Budget | fixed input count (2000 fn / 1000 prog) | wall-clock (1 min/method) |
132	| Deliverable | empirical metric + study | reusable per-method report + JaCoCo coverage |

145	| 3 | [gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) `<p> <dur>` | one Jazzer harness per manifest method |

161	
162	## Gotchas / limitations
163	
164	- **Fuzzing is sound for non-equivalence, incomplete for equivalence.** A DIVERGENT is a real witness;
165	  **EQUIVALENT only means "no divergence found in the budget," never a proof.** Trust it in proportion
166	  to the **Branch** column (`4/4` trustworthy; `0/0` branchless — read Line).
167	- **Coverage rewards new edges, not new disagreements** — value-only divergences with identical
168	  control flow get no search guidance (found only by luck).
169	- **Literal-only changes are invisible:** `strip_noise()` blanks string/char literal *contents*, so
170	  `return "alpha"` vs `return "beta"` normalizes identically and never enters the manifest. Verified.
171	- **Oracle is shallow:** exception *type* only (not messages), no side-effect / mutated-receiver
172	  comparison, non-comparable return types collapse to a null-ness check.
173	- **One finding halts the run** (AssertionError → Jazzer stops) — DIVERGENT logs are ~5 s, EQUIVALENT
174	  ~67 s. You get one divergence per method per run, not an enumeration.
175	- **Corpus lives under `target/`** → `mvn clean` or a fresh checkout wipes it; every method restarts
176	  from zero coverage. Move it outside `target/` to let coverage compound across sessions.
177	- **Rename artifacts:** `toString`/`hashCode` can show DIVERGENT purely because the class is renamed to
178	  `…Original`/`…Refactored`. Discard those.
179	- **Signature-changing refactorings** are out of scope (ERROR or dropped, per above).
180

```text
1	# Differential Fuzz Testing
2	
3	Project-level differential fuzz testing for identifying semantic preservation in software
4	refactoring: given the **original** and the **refactored** version of
5	a codebase, it finds the methods whose body changed, runs the original and refactored version of
6	each on the **same** [Jazzer](https://github.com/CodeIntelligenceTesting/jazzer)-generated inputs,
7	and reports where they disagree.
8	
9	- **Input:** two parallel source trees — `original/` and `refactored/` — with the same package layout.
10	- **Output:** a Markdown report classifying every changed, auto-fuzzable method as
11	  **EQUIVALENT / DIVERGENT / SKIP / ERROR**, with per-method branch/line coverage and, for each
12	  divergence, the reproducing input and the two differing outcomes.
13	
14	If for even one input the two versions differ (different return value, or different exception type),
15	the method is **DIVERGENT** — either a bug the refactoring introduced, or an intentional fix. That
16	is the finding the tool exists to surface.
17	
18	This is a standalone extraction of the differential-fuzzing work from the RefAgent replication
19	project. It has no dependency on RefAgent output or that repo's layout — you bring any
20	`original/` + `refactored/` pair.
21	
22	## Input contract
23	
24	```
25	original/                          refactored/
26	  com/acme/Foo.java                  com/acme/Foo.java
27	  com/acme/util/Bar.java             com/acme/util/Bar.java
28	```
29	
30	Files are paired by their path relative to each tree root. Only files present in **both** trees
31	are considered (a brand-new class has no original to diff against). For each pair the tool keeps
32	the methods whose body changed **and** whose parameters are all scalars it can synthesize from fuzz
33	bytes — primitives/boxes, `String`, and primitive arrays. Methods taking complex domain objects
34	are out of scope (excluded automatically).
35	
36	## Quick start (apex-core example)
37	
38	A worked example ships under [`examples/apex-core/`](examples/apex-core/): the `original/` and
39	`refactored/` trees for 27 apex-core classes, plus a [`sample-report.md`](examples/apex-core/sample-report.md).
40	
41	```bash
42	# 1. Provide the target project's own dependencies (apex-core needs the other apex classes).
43	#    The argument is a SEPARATE, already-built apex-core source checkout (mvn install -DskipTests) —
44	#    it must contain api/, common/, bufferserver/, engine/ each with a built target/classes.
45	#    This is NOT examples/apex-core (those are just the diff snapshots the tool fuzzes).
46	#    It installs the four modules as org.apache.apex.local:apex-*:3.7.0-local for the -Papex-core profile.
47	#    (First run only: chmod +x scripts/setup_deps.sh, or invoke it as `bash scripts/setup_deps.sh ...`.)
48	scripts/setup_deps.sh /path/to/built/apex-core
49	
50	# 2. Run the whole pipeline: two trees in, report out.
51	python3 run.py apex-core \
52	    --original   examples/apex-core/original \
53	    --refactored examples/apex-core/refactored
54	
55	# Smoke-test the first few methods only:
56	python3 run.py apex-core --original examples/apex-core/original \
57	    --refactored examples/apex-core/refactored --max 5
58	```
59	
60	The report lands at `reports/apex-core/auto-fuzz-report.md`.
61	
62	> **Requirements:** a JDK and Maven for the fuzzing steps. apex-core is a Java 8 project — build and
63	> run it on JDK 8. A Java 17 project must be built/run on JDK 21 (`export JAVA_HOME=...`); set its
64	> profile's `<maven.compiler.source|target>` to match. Step 1 (`build_project.py`) is pure Python.
65	
66	## What `run.py` does (the four steps)
67	
68	| Step | Script | What it produces |
69	|------|--------|------------------|
70	| 1 | `build_project.py <p> --original <o> --refactored <r>` | `manifest.json` + renamed `<Class>{Original,Refactored}` snapshots |
71	| 2 | `prune.py <p>` | iterative `mvn -P<p> test-compile`; drops class pairs whose deps don't resolve |
72	| 3 | `gen_harnesses.py <p> <dur>` | one thin Jazzer harness per manifest method |
73	| 4 | `run_project.py <p>` | fuzzes each method + JaCoCo coverage → `reports/<p>/auto-fuzz-report.md` |
74	
75	Steps 1, 3, 4 are pure per-project; step 2 needs the project's dependencies on the classpath.
76	You can run steps individually, or all at once via `run.py`.
77	
78	## Reading the report
79	
80	- **DIVERGENT** — the two versions differ on some input (exception type or return value). The real
81	  finding; triage each as bug vs intentional fix. To see the proof:
82	  ```bash
83	  grep -A5 -F "[DIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH]" target/fuzz-logs/<project>/<Class>_<method>.log
84	  ```
85	  The block prints `methodArgs` (the reproducing input) and both `original` / `refactored` outcomes.
86	- **EQUIVALENT** — no divergence found in the time budget. Trust it in proportion to the **Branch**
87	  column: `4/4` = both outcomes of every decision were exercised; `0/0` = branchless (read the Line
88	  column); low branch = under-explored, not proven equivalent.
89	- **SKIP** — instance method whose receiver couldn't be constructed generically (abstract/interface,
90	  or no usable constructor).
91	- **ERROR** — ran but couldn't be tested (e.g. the constructor throws at runtime).
92	
93	## Add your own project
94	
95	1. Put your two source trees anywhere (e.g. `examples/<project>/{original,refactored}`).
96	2. Make the project's dependencies resolvable — add a `<profile id="<project>">` in
97	   [`pom.xml`](pom.xml) (copy the `apex-core` profile: change the id, list your project's
98	   dependencies, and point the two `add-test-source` paths at `src/test/Dataset/<project>` and
99	   `src/test/fuzzing/<project>`).
100	3. `python3 run.py <project> --original <o> --refactored <r>`. `prune.py` auto-drops whatever
101	   won't compile.
102	
103	## Layout
104	
105	```
106	run.py                                   one entry point: two trees -> report
107	pom.xml                                  engine-only base; one <profile> per target project
108	scripts/
109	  build_project.py                       (1) two-tree diff -> manifest + snapshots
110	  prune.py                               (2) compile-and-drop gate
111	  gen_harnesses.py                       (3) one Jazzer harness per method
112	  run_project.py                         (4) fuzz + coverage -> report
113	  auto_select.py                         shared Java-parsing helpers
114	  CovReport.java                         JaCoCo per-method branch/line extractor
115	  setup_deps.sh                          install a project's built classes as local Maven jars
116	src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java   the shared reflection engine + oracle
117	examples/apex-core/{original,refactored}/          worked example input trees
118	examples/apex-core/sample-report.md                what the output looks like
119	```
120	
121	`src/test/Dataset/`, `src/test/fuzzing/`, `src/test/resources/`, `reports/`, and `target/` are all
122	generated by the pipeline and git-ignored — regenerate them with `run.py`.
123	
124	## How the oracle decides (and its limits)
125	
126	The engine builds the receiver and arguments from Jazzer's `FuzzedDataProvider`, invokes both
127	versions via reflection on a **3-second per-call watchdog** (a runaway input becomes a TIMEOUT, not
128	a stall), and compares. Different **exception type**, or different scalar/JDK **return value**, =
129	DIVERGENT. A one-sided TIMEOUT is treated as inconclusive, not divergent.
130	
131	The oracle is deliberately shallow: it compares return value + exception *type* only — not exception
132	messages, deep object equality, or side effects. Fuzzing is nondeterministic, so the authoritative
133	record of a divergence is the report row plus the log line still containing `[DIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH]`;
134	`methodArgs` lets you reproduce it by hand.
135
```

```md
# Context — Differential Fuzz Testing (working notes)

> Git-ignored scratch context for Claude sessions. Not a deliverable. The user-facing docs are
> [README.md](README.md); the richer session narrative is [handoff.md](handoff.md) (also git-ignored,
> intentionally never committed per its provenance notes).

## What this project is (one paragraph)

A **standalone differential-fuzzing tool for refactorings**. You give it two parallel Java source
trees — `original/` and `refactored/` with the same package layout — and it finds every method whose
body changed, runs the original and refactored versions on the **same** Jazzer-generated inputs, and
emits a Markdown report classifying each changed, auto-fuzzable method as **EQUIVALENT / DIVERGENT /
SKIP / ERROR**. A DIVERGENT method is a real witness of behavior change (a bug the refactoring
introduced, or an intentional fix). It's an extraction from the RefAgent replication project, with no
dependency on RefAgent. Derived from Dristi & Dwyer, arXiv **2602.15761** (UVA), *"A Differential
Fuzzing-Based Evaluation of Functional Equivalence in LLM-Generated Code Refactorings."*

## Architecture (important, was a point of confusion)

- **Symmetric single-harness design**, NOT directed/generate-then-replay. Both versions are invoked
  in the *same* fuzz iteration on the *same* input; coverage guidance uses the **union** of both
  instrumented versions. (A `--regression` replay mode exists but is not the default.)
- Fuzzer: **Jazzer** (libFuzzer-based, coverage-guided). Sibling of the paper's Atheris.
- Granularity: **individual changed method**, source-diffed. The paper works at whole-function level.

## The pipeline — one entry point `run.py <project>` chains 4 steps

| Step | Script | Produces |
|------|--------|----------|
| 1 | [scripts/build_project.py](scripts/build_project.py) `<p> --original <o> --refactored <r>` | `manifest.json` + renamed `<Class>{Original,Refactored}.java` snapshots |
| 2 | [scripts/prune.py](scripts/prune.py) `<p>` | iterative `mvn -P<p> test-compile`; drops pairs that won't compile (rewrites manifest) |
| 3 | [scripts/gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) `<p> <dur>` | one Jazzer harness per manifest method |
| 4 | [scripts/run_project.py](scripts/run_project.py) `<p>` | fuzz + JaCoCo coverage → `reports/<p>/auto-fuzz-report.md` |

Shared helper: [scripts/auto_select.py](scripts/auto_select.py) (Java-signature parsing + `classify()`).
Coverage extractor: [scripts/CovReport.java](scripts/CovReport.java). Dep installer:
[scripts/setup_deps.sh](scripts/setup_deps.sh).

## How it works (distilled)

- **Manifest creation**: pairs files by relative path → heuristic regex+brace-matcher parses each
  side's top-level methods → keeps a method iff it exists in **both** trees with **same name+arity**
  but a **changed normalized body** → keeps only **auto-fuzzable** ones (every param scalar / String /
  primitive array) → writes `manifest.json` + `<Class>{Original,Refactored}.java` into the **same
  package** so both compile into one JVM.
- **Signature source**: `params` + `static` read from the **refactored** signature
  ([build_project.py:87](scripts/build_project.py#L87)). Return type for comparability read from the
  **original** method. Name+arity shared by construction. Verified 0 signature disagreements across
  apex-core, so it doesn't matter in practice.
- **Fuzz loop** ([src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java)):
  Jazzer drives a thin per-method harness → resolves both `Original`/`Refactored` classes → builds
  receiver (recursive ctor synthesis for instance methods) + args once from `FuzzedDataProvider` using
  manifest `params` as decode schema → `copy()`s per side → invokes each on a **3 s watchdog thread**
  → oracle compares.
- **Oracle** (`equivalent()`): DIVERGENT iff exception **types** differ, or (neither threw)
  scalar/JDK **return values** differ. One-sided **TIMEOUT = inconclusive** (not divergent).

## Repo / provenance state

- Canonical private repo: `git@github.com:musta55/Differential-Fuzz-Testing.git`. 2-commit history:
  `9e661d5` (project) on top of `08e03c7` (GitHub Initial commit + MIT LICENSE). Author = user only,
  no Claude co-author trailer, no RefAgent history. `handoff.md`/`context.md` are NOT in the repo.
- Local working copy currently on branch `main`, clean (before this session's `.gitignore` +
  `context.md` changes).
- Generated + git-ignored (regenerate with `run.py`): `src/test/Dataset/`, `src/test/fuzzing/`,
  `src/test/resources/`, `reports/`, `target/`.

## Last recorded run (apex-core, 27 classes → 62 methods)

**EQUIVALENT 34 · DIVERGENT 11 · SKIP 14 · ERROR 3.** Worked divergence example:
`VersionInfo.compare` — refactoring dropped two empty-string guards → original `returns 1`, refactored
`throws NumberFormatException` on `str1="5$", str2=""`. See
[examples/apex-core/sample-report.md](examples/apex-core/sample-report.md).

## Requirements

JDK + Maven for fuzzing steps. apex-core is Java 8 → build/run on JDK 8. A Java 17 project → JDK 21.
Step 1 is pure Python.

## Key limitations (trust EQUIVALENT with care)

- **Sound for non-equivalence, incomplete for equivalence** — EQUIVALENT only means "no divergence
  found in budget," never a proof. Trust in proportion to the **Branch** coverage column.
- **Coverage rewards new edges, not new disagreements** — value-only divergences with identical
  control flow are found only by luck. (Deepest current weakness; Jazzer custom-feedback hooks could
  fix it.)
- **Literal-only changes invisible**: `strip_noise()` blanks string/char literal contents, so
  `return "alpha"` vs `"beta"` normalizes identically and never enters the manifest.
- **Shallow oracle**: exception *type* only (not messages), no side-effect / mutated-receiver
  comparison; non-comparable return types collapse to a null-ness check.
- **Non-scalar params dropped at manifest time** (no complex-object synthesis).
- **Signature-changing refactorings** out of scope: type change → runtime ERROR (fail-safe); arity
  change → pair dropped (blind spot, but never a false EQUIVALENT).
- **One finding halts the run** (AssertionError stops Jazzer) — one divergence/method/run, not an
  enumeration. **Corpus lives under `target/`** → `mvn clean` wipes it.
- **Rename artifacts**: `toString`/`hashCode` can show DIVERGENT purely from the `…Original`/
  `…Refactored` rename — discard those.

## Open decisions (the fork to resolve first)

1. **Project goal** drives everything — two mutually-exclusive directions:
   - **Faithful reproduction of the paper** → reimplement in **Python** over HumanEval/MBPP/APPS with
     **Atheris**, whole-function granularity, GPT-inferred input constraints (to match their tables).
     Current Java/method-level tool would NOT reproduce their numbers.
   - **New Java tool / thesis extension** → **keep** current design; its differentiator is exactly the
     Java + method-level + source-diffing the paper can't do.
2. If extending: highest-value upgrades are **input-constraint inference** (past the scalar-only limit)
   and **divergence-directed feedback** (reward disagreement, not just new coverage edges).
3. Local working-copy origin repoint vs. fresh clone (minor; see handoff.md).

## Paper comparison headline

LLMs produce **19–35% non-equivalent** refactorings; **~21%** of those still pass the datasets'
existing test suites (tests overestimate equivalence).

## Project summary: Differential Fuzz Testing

**What it is.** A standalone tool that checks whether a **refactoring preserved behavior**. You hand it two parallel Java source trees — `original/` and `refactored/` with identical package layout — and it finds every method whose *body* changed, runs both versions on the **same** [Jazzer](https://github.com/CodeIntelligenceTesting/jazzer)-generated inputs, and produces a Markdown report classifying each method as **EQUIVALENT / DIVERGENT / SKIP / ERROR**. A DIVERGENT method is a concrete witness that behavior changed — a bug the refactoring introduced, or an intentional fix.

It's a clean extraction from the RefAgent replication project (no dependency on it), derived from the approach in Dristi & Dwyer, arXiv **2602.15761** (UVA).

**How it works — 4 steps chained by [run.py](run.py):**

| # | Script | Produces |
|---|--------|----------|
| 1 | [build_project.py](scripts/build_project.py) | Diffs the two trees → `manifest.json` + renamed `<Class>{Original,Refactored}.java` snapshots (same package, one JVM) |
| 2 | [prune.py](scripts/prune.py) | `mvn test-compile`; drops pairs that won't compile |
| 3 | [gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) | One thin Jazzer harness per method |
| 4 | [run_project.py](scripts/run_project.py) | Fuzzes each method + JaCoCo coverage → `reports/<p>/auto-fuzz-report.md` |

The engine is [GenericDifferential.java](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java): it builds a receiver (recursive constructor synthesis) and args from Jazzer's byte stream, invokes both versions on a **3 s watchdog**, and the oracle flags DIVERGENT when **exception types** or **scalar return values** differ. One-sided TIMEOUT = inconclusive.

**Key design point** (a corrected misconception in the handoff): it's a **symmetric single-harness** design — both versions run in the *same* iteration on the *same* input, coverage-guided by the **union** of both — *not* a directed generate-then-replay design.

**Ships with** a worked apex-core example (27 classes → 62 methods). Last run: **EQUIVALENT 34 · DIVERGENT 11 · SKIP 14 · ERROR 3**. The showcase divergence is `VersionInfo.compare`, where dropping two empty-string guards turned `return 1` into a `NumberFormatException`.

**Main limitations to keep in mind:** sound for non-equivalence but *incomplete* for equivalence (EQUIVALENT ≠ proof — trust it in proportion to branch coverage); scalar/String/primitive-array params only (complex objects dropped); shallow oracle (exception *type* only, no messages/side-effects); coverage rewards new edges, not new *disagreements*; and one finding halts the run.

**The open fork** (per the handoff, still undecided) is the project's *goal*: faithfully **reproduce the paper** (would require a Python/Atheris/whole-function rewrite) vs. **extend this Java tool** as a thesis contribution (its differentiator is exactly the Java + method-level + source-diffing the paper can't do).

I distilled all of this — architecture, pipeline, run state, limitations, and the open decisions — into [context.md](context.md) for future sessions. Want me to actually run the pipeline on the apex-core example to confirm it still works end-to-end, or dig into resolving that goal fork?

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Pure Java-parsing helpers shared by build_project.py.
4	
5	A heuristic parser (strip comments + literals, then brace-match) that extracts each
6	top-level method's normalized body + signature, and classifies whether every parameter
7	type is a scalar the GenericDifferential engine can synthesize from fuzz bytes
8	(primitives/boxes, String, primitive arrays). No project layout is assumed here — the
9	functions take Java source text and paths only.
10	"""
11	import re
12	
13	KEYWORDS = {"if", "for", "while", "switch", "catch", "synchronized", "return",
14	            "new", "else", "do", "try", "finally", "case"}
15	
16	PRIMS = {"int", "long", "short", "byte", "char", "boolean", "float", "double"}
17	SCALAR = PRIMS | {"String"} | {p + "[]" for p in PRIMS}
18	
19	SIG_RE = re.compile(
20	    r'(?P<sig>(?P<pre>(?:[A-Za-z_$][\w$<>\[\],.\s?&]*?\s+)?)'
21	    r'(?P<name>[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*'
22	    r'\((?P<params>[^;{}]*)\)\s*'
23	    r'(?:throws\s[\w$.,\s]+?)?)\s*\{',
24	)
25	
26	
27	def strip_noise(src):
28	    out, i, n = [], 0, len(src)
29	    while i < n:
30	        c, two = src[i], src[i:i + 2]
31	        if two == "//":
32	            j = src.find("\n", i); i = n if j < 0 else j; continue
33	        if two == "/*":
34	            j = src.find("*/", i + 2); i = n if j < 0 else j + 2; continue
35	        if c == '"':
36	            j = i + 1
37	            while j < n and src[j] != '"':
38	                j += 2 if src[j] == "\\" else 1
39	            out.append('""'); i = j + 1; continue
40	        if c == "'":
41	            j = i + 1
42	            while j < n and src[j] != "'":
43	                j += 2 if src[j] == "\\" else 1
44	            out.append("' '"); i = j + 1; continue
45	        out.append(c); i += 1
46	    return "".join(out)
47	
48	
49	def methods(src):
50	    """name/paramCount -> (normalized_body, pre_modifiers, params_str). Top-level methods only."""
51	    clean = strip_noise(src)
52	    out = {}
53	    for m in SIG_RE.finditer(clean):
54	        name = m.group("name")
55	        if name in KEYWORDS:
56	            continue
57	        brace = clean.find("{", m.start())
58	        # Only top-level methods (primary class body == brace depth 1) can be addressed as
59	        # <PrimaryClass>.method; methods in a nested class/enum are at depth >= 2 -> skip.
60	        if clean.count("{", 0, brace) - clean.count("}", 0, brace) != 1:
61	            continue
62	        depth, j, n = 0, brace, len(clean)
63	        while j < n:
64	            if clean[j] == "{": depth += 1
65	            elif clean[j] == "}":
66	                depth -= 1
67	                if depth == 0: break
68	            j += 1
69	        params = m.group("params").strip()
70	        pcount = 0 if not params else len(split_params(params))
71	        key = f"{name}/{pcount}"
72	        base, k = key, 0
73	        while key in out:
74	            k += 1; key = f"{base}#{k}"
75	        out[key] = (re.sub(r"\s+", " ", clean[brace:j + 1]).strip(),
76	                    m.group("pre").strip(), params)
77	    return out
78	
79	
80	def split_params(params):
81	    parts, depth, cur = [], 0, ""
82	    for ch in params:
83	        if ch == "<": depth += 1
84	        elif ch == ">": depth -= 1
85	        if ch == "," and depth == 0:
86	            parts.append(cur); cur = ""
87	        else:
88	            cur += ch
89	    if cur.strip():
90	        parts.append(cur)
91	    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]
92	
93	
94	def param_type(p):
95	    """Extract the (type) token of a single 'Type name' parameter, or None if not scalar."""
96	    if "<" in p or "@" in p or "..." in p:
97	        return None
98	    toks = [t for t in p.replace("\t", " ").split() if t != "final"]
99	    if len(toks) < 2:
100	        return None
101	    return toks[-2]  # token before the parameter name
102	
103	
104	def classify(pre, params):
105	    """Return (auto_fuzzable, is_static, [typeTokens]) for a method signature."""
106	    is_static = bool(re.search(r"\bstatic\b", pre))
107	    if not params:
108	        return True, is_static, []
109	    types = []
110	    for p in split_params(params):
111	        t = param_type(p)
112	        if t is None or t not in SCALAR:
113	            return False, is_static, []
114	        types.append(t)
115	    return True, is_static, types
116	
117	
118	def package(path):
119	    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
120	        m = re.match(r"\s*package\s+([\w.]+)\s*;", line)
121	        if m:
122	            return m.group(1)
123	    return None
124

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Build the manifest + compiled-source snapshots for a project from two parallel source trees.
4	
5	INPUT CONTRACT (decoupled — no RefAgent/results layout assumed):
6	    build_project.py <project> --original <origTree> --refactored <refTree>
7	
8	  <origTree> and <refTree> are two source trees with the SAME package structure, e.g.
9	      original/com/acme/Foo.java     refactored/com/acme/Foo.java
10	  Files are paired by their path relative to each tree root. A file present only in the
11	  refactored tree (a brand-new class) is skipped: there is no original to diff against.
12	
13	For each paired class we find the methods whose body changed, keep the AUTO_FUZZABLE ones
14	(scalar/String/array args, top-level — see auto_select.classify), and:
15	  - copy the original file  -> src/test/Dataset/<project>/<pkg>/<Class>Original.java   (renamed)
16	  - copy the refactored file -> src/test/Dataset/<project>/<pkg>/<Class>Refactored.java (renamed)
17	  - record a manifest entry {id, original FQN, refactored FQN, method, params, static}
18	
19	Writes src/test/resources/<project>/manifest.json (read at fuzz time by GenericDifferential).
20	The whole-word rename also fixes self-references (e.g. `VersionInfo x = new VersionInfo()`).
21	"""
22	import argparse
23	import os
24	import re
25	import sys
26	
27	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
28	from auto_select import methods, classify, package  # noqa: E402
29	
30	MODULE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
31	
32	JAVA_FQN = {"String": "java.lang.String"}  # primitives + primitive arrays pass through
33	
34	
35	def java_type(t):
36	    return JAVA_FQN.get(t, t)
37	
38	
39	def rename(text, cls, suffix):
40	    """Whole-word rename of the class's own name (handles decl, ctors, self-refs, .class)."""
41	    return re.sub(r"\b" + re.escape(cls) + r"\b", cls + suffix, text)
42	
43	
44	def pair_files(orig_root, ref_root):
45	    """Yield (rel_path, orig_abs, ref_abs) for every .java present in BOTH trees."""
46	    for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(ref_root):
47	        for f in files:
48	            if not f.endswith(".java"):
49	                continue
50	            ref_abs = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
51	            rel = os.path.relpath(ref_abs, ref_root)
52	            orig_abs = os.path.join(orig_root, rel)
53	            if os.path.isfile(orig_abs):
54	                yield rel, orig_abs, ref_abs
55	
56	
57	def main(project, orig_root, ref_root):
58	    orig_root = os.path.abspath(orig_root)
59	    ref_root = os.path.abspath(ref_root)
60	    for label, root in (("--original", orig_root), ("--refactored", ref_root)):
61	        if not os.path.isdir(root):
62	            print(f"ERROR: {label} tree not found: {root}", file=sys.stderr)
63	            return 1
64	
65	    java_root = os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/Dataset", project)  # per-project source root
66	    entries = []
67	    seen = {}
68	    n_classes = 0
69	
70	    for rel, orig_p, ref_p in sorted(pair_files(orig_root, ref_root)):
71	        cls = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(ref_p))[0]  # filename stem == public class name
72	        orig_txt = open(orig_p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
73	        impr_txt = open(ref_p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
74	        pkg = package(ref_p)
75	        if not pkg:
76	            continue
77	        o = methods(orig_txt)
78	        n = methods(impr_txt)
79	
80	        class_entries = []
81	        for key in n:
82	            if key not in o or o[key][0] == n[key][0]:
83	                continue  # unchanged or added-only
84	            name = key.split("/")[0].split("#")[0]
85	            if name == cls:

87	            ok, is_static, types = classify(n[key][1], n[key][2])
88	            if not ok:
89	                continue  # NEEDS_OBJECT
90	            mid = f"{cls}.{name}"
91	            if mid in seen:
92	                seen[mid] += 1
93	                mid = f"{mid}_{seen[mid]}"
94	            else:
95	                seen[mid] = 0
96	            class_entries.append({
97	                "id": mid,
98	                "original": f"{pkg}.{cls}Original",
99	                "refactored": f"{pkg}.{cls}Refactored",
100	                "method": name,
101	                "params": [java_type(t) for t in types],
102	                "static": is_static,
103	            })
104	
105	        if not class_entries:
106	            continue
107	
108	        pkg_dir = os.path.join(java_root, pkg.replace(".", "/"))
109	        os.makedirs(pkg_dir, exist_ok=True)
110	        open(os.path.join(pkg_dir, f"{cls}Original.java"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(rename(orig_txt, cls, "Original"))
111	        open(os.path.join(pkg_dir, f"{cls}Refactored.java"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(rename(impr_txt, cls, "Refactored"))
112	        entries.extend(class_entries)
113	        n_classes += 1
114	
115	    res_dir = os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/resources", project)
116	    os.makedirs(res_dir, exist_ok=True)
117	    import json
118	    with open(os.path.join(res_dir, "manifest.json"), "w") as f:
119	        json.dump({"project": project, "source": {"original": orig_root, "refactored": ref_root},
120	                   "methods": entries}, f, indent=2)
121	
122	    print(f"{project}: {n_classes} classes, {len(entries)} auto-fuzzable methods")
123	    print(f"  sources  -> src/test/Dataset/{project}/<pkg>/<Class>{{Original,Refactored}}.java")
124	    print(f"  manifest -> src/test/resources/{project}/manifest.json")
125	    return 0
126	
127	
128	if __name__ == "__main__":
129	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build manifest + snapshots from two source trees.")
130	    ap.add_argument("project")
131	    ap.add_argument("--original", required=True, help="original source tree root")
132	    ap.add_argument("--refactored", required=True, help="refactored source tree root")
133	    args = ap.parse_args()
134	    sys.exit(main(args.project, args.original, args.refactored))

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Iteratively `mvn test-compile` and drop any <Class>{Original,Refactored} pair that fails to
4	compile (missing project deps), plus its manifest entries, until the build is clean.
5	
6	This is the per-class dependency gate, automated: classes whose deps aren't on the
7	classpath are skipped (add the dep to pom.xml later to recover them).
8	
9	Usage: prune.py <project> [maxRounds=30]
10	"""
11	import json
12	import os
13	import re
14	import subprocess
15	import sys
16	
17	MODULE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
18	
19	
20	def failing_class_files(output):
21	    """Return {(dir, classBase)} for every <ClassBase>{Original,Refactored}.java in errors."""
22	    out = set()
23	    for m in re.finditer(r"(/\S+?)/(\w+?)(Original|Refactored)\.java:\[", output):
24	        out.add((m.group(1), m.group(2)))
25	    return out
26	
27	
28	def filter_manifest(project, removed_bases):
29	    path = os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/resources", project, "manifest.json")
30	    data = json.load(open(path))
31	    before = len(data["methods"])
32	    kept = []
33	    for e in data["methods"]:
34	        base = e["refactored"].split(".")[-1][:-len("Refactored")]
35	        if base not in removed_bases:
36	            kept.append(e)
37	    data["methods"] = kept
38	    json.dump(data, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
39	    return before - len(kept)
40	
41	
42	def main(project, max_rounds):
43	    all_removed = set()
44	    for rnd in range(max_rounds):
45	        p = subprocess.run(["mvn", f"-P{project}", "test-compile"], cwd=MODULE, capture_output=True, text=True)
46	        out = p.stdout + p.stderr
47	        if "BUILD SUCCESS" in out:
48	            print(f"compile clean after {rnd} prune round(s). pruned classes: {len(all_removed)}")
49	            if all_removed:
50	                print("  pruned:", " ".join(sorted(all_removed)))
51	            return 0
52	        fails = failing_class_files(out)
53	        if not fails:
54	            print("BUILD FAILURE but no <Class>{Original,Refactored} file in errors — manual look:")
55	            print("\n".join(l for l in out.splitlines() if "ERROR" in l)[:2000])
56	            return 1
57	        bases = set()
58	        for d, base in fails:
59	            for suf in ("Original", "Refactored"):
60	                f = os.path.join(d, base + suf + ".java")
61	                if os.path.exists(f):
62	                    os.remove(f)
63	            bases.add(base)
64	        dropped = filter_manifest(project, bases)
65	        all_removed |= bases
66	        print(f"  round {rnd}: removed {len(bases)} class(es), {dropped} manifest entries -> {sorted(bases)}")
67	    print("hit max rounds; still failing")
68	    return 1
69	
70	
71	if __name__ == "__main__":
72	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
73	        print(__doc__)
74	        sys.exit(2)
75	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 30))

3	import java.io.InputStreamReader;
4	import java.io.Reader;

6	import java.lang.reflect.Method;
7	import java.util.Arrays;
8	import java.util.HashMap;
9	import java.util.Map;
10	import java.util.Objects;
11	import java.util.concurrent.FutureTask;
12	import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
13	import java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException;

15	import com.code_intelligence.jazzer.api.FuzzedDataProvider;
16	import com.google.gson.JsonArray;
17	import com.google.gson.JsonObject;
18	import com.google.gson.JsonParser;

20	import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions;
21	
22	/**
23	 * Reflection-based differential oracle, driven by a per-project JSON manifest.
24	 *
25	 * A thin generated harness calls {@link #run(FuzzedDataProvider, String, String)} with its
26	 * project and method id; this engine looks the spec up in
27	 * {@code /<project>/manifest.json} (on the test classpath), resolves the compiled
28	 * {@code <Class>Original} and {@code <Class>Refactored} snapshots, builds the SAME args from
29	 * the fuzzer for both, invokes each (on a 3s watchdog thread), and asserts equivalence.
30	 *
31	 * Equivalence: DIVERGENT iff the two sides differ in exception TYPE (e.g. NPE vs
32	 * ArrayIndexOutOfBounds) or in scalar/String return value. A one-sided TIMEOUT (watchdog)
33	 * is treated as inconclusive (NOT divergent) since it is timing-dependent.
34	 */
35	public final class GenericDifferential
36	{
37	  private GenericDifferential() {}
38	
39	  private static final long CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = Long.getLong("fuzz.callTimeoutMs", 3000L);
40	
41	  // ── entry point used by the generated harnesses ─────────────────────────────
42	
43	  public static void run(FuzzedDataProvider data, String project, String id) throws Throwable
44	  {
45	    Spec s = spec(project, id);
46	    Class<?> oCls = Class.forName(s.original);
47	    Class<?> rCls = Class.forName(s.refactored);
48	    Method oM = method(oCls, s.method, s.paramTypes);
49	    Method rM = method(rCls, s.method, s.paramTypes);
50	    oM.setAccessible(true);
51	    rM.setAccessible(true);
52	
53	    // Build the receiver FIRST (consumes ctor args from the fuzzer), then the method args,
54	    // so both sides get identical inputs throughout.
55	    Object oInst = null;
56	    Object rInst = null;
57	    String ctorDesc = "(static)";
58	    if (!s.isStatic) {
59	      Object[] built;
60	      try {
61	        built = construct(oCls, rCls, data);
62	      } catch (CannotConstruct e) {
63	        // No constructor can be synthesized from fuzz data (even recursively) — structural
64	        // skip. Print the marker and rethrow so Jazzer stops this target fast (no 1-min no-op).
65	        System.out.println("[SKIP] cannot construct " + s.original + " (" + e.getMessage() + ")");
66	        throw e;
67	      }
68	      if (built == null) {
69	        return; // a buildable ctor rejected THIS input — let Jazzer try another input
70	      }
71	      oInst = built[0];
72	      rInst = built[1];
73	      ctorDesc = (String) built[2];
74	    }
75	    Object[] base = buildArgs(data, s.paramTypes);
76	
77	    Outcome o = invokeTimed(oM, oInst, copy(base));
78	    Outcome r = invokeTimed(rM, rInst, copy(base));
79	
80	    if (!equivalent(o, r, oM.getReturnType())) {
81	      Assertions.fail(String.format(
82	          "[DIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH] %s.%s%s%n  ctorArgs  : %s%n  methodArgs: %s%n"
83	          + "  original  : %s%n  refactored: %s",
84	          s.original.substring(s.original.lastIndexOf('.') + 1), s.method,
85	          Arrays.toString(s.paramTypes), ctorDesc, render(base), o, r));
86	    }
87	  }
88	
89	  // ── manifest ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
90	
91	  private static final Map<String, Map<String, Spec>> CACHE = new HashMap<>();
92	
93	  private static final class Spec
94	  {
95	    String original;
96	    String refactored;
97	    String method;
98	    Class<?>[] paramTypes;
99	    boolean isStatic;
100	  }
101	
102	  private static synchronized Spec spec(String project, String id) throws Exception
103	  {
104	    Map<String, Spec> byId = CACHE.get(project);
105	    if (byId == null) {
106	      byId = new HashMap<>();
107	      String path = "/" + project + "/manifest.json";
108	      try (Reader r = new InputStreamReader(
109	          Objects.requireNonNull(GenericDifferential.class.getResourceAsStream(path),
110	              "manifest not found on classpath: " + path), "UTF-8")) {
111	        JsonObject root = JsonParser.parseReader(r).getAsJsonObject();
112	        JsonArray methods = root.getAsJsonArray("methods");
113	        for (int i = 0; i < methods.size(); i++) {
114	          JsonObject m = methods.get(i).getAsJsonObject();
115	          Spec sp = new Spec();
116	          sp.original = m.get("original").getAsString();
117	          sp.refactored = m.get("refactored").getAsString();
118	          sp.method = m.get("method").getAsString();
119	          sp.isStatic = m.get("static").getAsBoolean();
120	          JsonArray ps = m.getAsJsonArray("params");
121	          Class<?>[] pts = new Class<?>[ps.size()];
122	          for (int j = 0; j < ps.size(); j++) {
123	            pts[j] = classFor(ps.get(j).getAsString());
124	          }
125	          sp.paramTypes = pts;
126	          byId.put(m.get("id").getAsString(), sp);
127	        }
128	      }
129	      CACHE.put(project, byId);
130	    }
131	    Spec s = byId.get(id);
132	    if (s == null) {
133	      throw new IllegalStateException("id not in manifest: " + project + "/" + id);
134	    }
135	    return s;
136	  }
137	
138	  // ── invocation + oracle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
139	
140	  private static final class Outcome
141	  {
142	    final Object value;
143	    final String exception;
144	    Outcome(Object v, String ex) { value = v; exception = ex; }
145	    boolean threw() { return exception != null; }
146	    @Override public String toString() { return threw() ? "throws " + exception : "returns " + render(value); }
147	  }
148	
149	  private static Outcome invoke(Method m, Object inst, Object[] args)
150	  {
151	    try {
152	      return new Outcome(m.invoke(inst, args), null);
153	    } catch (InvocationTargetException e) {
154	      Throwable c = e.getCause() != null ? e.getCause() : e;
155	      return new Outcome(null, c.getClass().getSimpleName());
156	    } catch (Throwable t) {
157	      return new Outcome(null, t.getClass().getSimpleName());
158	    }
159	  }
160	
161	  private static Outcome invokeTimed(Method m, Object inst, Object[] args)
162	  {
163	    FutureTask<Outcome> task = new FutureTask<>(() -> invoke(m, inst, args));
164	    Thread t = new Thread(task, "diff-invoke");
165	    t.setDaemon(true);
166	    t.start();
167	    try {
168	      return task.get(CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
169	    } catch (TimeoutException te) {
170	      t.interrupt();
171	      return new Outcome(null, "TIMEOUT");
172	    } catch (Throwable e) {
173	      Throwable c = e.getCause() != null ? e.getCause() : e;
174	      return new Outcome(null, c.getClass().getSimpleName());
175	    }
176	  }
177	
178	  /**
179	   * DIVERGENT iff exception types differ OR (neither threw) scalar/JDK return values differ.
180	   * A one-sided TIMEOUT is inconclusive (timing-dependent) → treated as NOT divergent so the
181	   * watchdog can't manufacture false positives on slow/ReDoS inputs.
182	   */
183	  private static boolean equivalent(Outcome o, Outcome r, Class<?> returnType)
184	  {
185	    boolean oTo = "TIMEOUT".equals(o.exception);
186	    boolean rTo = "TIMEOUT".equals(r.exception);
187	    if (oTo || rTo) {
188	      return true; // inconclusive, not a reliable divergence
189	    }
190	    if (!Objects.equals(o.exception, r.exception)) {
191	      return false; // different exception type (e.g. NPE vs AIOOBE) → DIVERGENT
192	    }
193	    if (o.threw()) {
194	      return true;
195	    }
196	    if (returnType == void.class) {
197	      return true;
198	    }
199	    if (isComparable(returnType)) {
200	      return deepEquals(o.value, r.value);
201	    }
202	    return (o.value == null) == (r.value == null);
203	  }
204	
205	  private static boolean isComparable(Class<?> t)
206	  {
207	    return t.isPrimitive() || t == String.class || Number.class.isAssignableFrom(t)
208	        || t == Boolean.class || t == Character.class || t.isEnum()
209	        || (t.isArray() && t.getComponentType().isPrimitive());
210	  }
211	
212	  // ── reflection helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
213	
214	  private static Method method(Class<?> c, String name, Class<?>[] params) throws NoSuchMethodException
215	  {
216	    try {
217	      return c.getDeclaredMethod(name, params);
218	    } catch (NoSuchMethodException e) {
219	      return c.getMethod(name, params);
220	    }
221	  }
222	
223	  /**
224	   * Build matching receiver instances for original + refactored, sharing the SAME fuzzer-built
225	   * constructor arguments. Prefers a no-arg ctor, else the smallest ctor whose params are all
226	   * fuzz-buildable (scalar/String/array) and that BOTH classes declare. Returns {oInst, rInst}
227	   * or null if none works (or the ctor throws for this input).
228	   */
229	  /** No constructor can be synthesized (even recursively) — structural skip. */
230	  private static final class CannotConstruct extends RuntimeException
231	  {
232	    CannotConstruct(String m) { super(m); }
233	  }
234	
235	  /** A required constructor-parameter type couldn't be built from fuzz data. */
236	  private static final class CannotBuild extends RuntimeException
237	  {
238	    CannotBuild(String m) { super(m); }
239	  }
240	
241	  /**
242	   * Build matching receiver instances for original + refactored, sharing the SAME fuzzer-built
243	   * constructor arguments. Tries each constructor smallest-first; a parameter is a scalar
244	   * (built directly) or another object built recursively (depth-limited). Returns
245	   * {oInst, rInst, ctorArgsDesc}; returns null if a buildable ctor rejected THIS input;
246	   * throws CannotConstruct if no constructor can be synthesized at all.
247	   */
248	  private static Object[] construct(Class<?> oCls, Class<?> rCls, FuzzedDataProvider d)
249	  {
250	    java.lang.reflect.Constructor<?>[] ctors = oCls.getDeclaredConstructors();
251	    Arrays.sort(ctors, java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(java.lang.reflect.Constructor::getParameterCount));
252	    for (java.lang.reflect.Constructor<?> oc : ctors) {
253	      if (java.lang.reflect.Modifier.isPrivate(oc.getModifiers())) {
254	        continue;
255	      }
256	      Class<?>[] pts = oc.getParameterTypes();
257	      java.lang.reflect.Constructor<?> rc;
258	      try {
259	        rc = rCls.getDeclaredConstructor(pts);
260	      } catch (NoSuchMethodException e) {
261	        continue; // refactored ctor signature differs — try another
262	      }
263	      Object[] cargs;
264	      try {
265	        cargs = buildCtorArgs(d, pts, 2);
266	      } catch (CannotBuild e) {
267	        continue; // can't synthesize a parameter — try another constructor
268	      }
269	      oc.setAccessible(true);
270	      rc.setAccessible(true);
271	      try {
272	        Object o = oc.newInstance(copy(cargs));
273	        Object r = rc.newInstance(copy(cargs));
274	        return new Object[]{o, r, render(cargs)};
275	      } catch (Throwable t) {
276	        return null; // ctor exists + buildable but rejected this input — try another input
277	      }
278	    }
279	    throw new CannotConstruct("no buildable constructor");
280	  }
281	
282	  private static Object[] buildCtorArgs(FuzzedDataProvider d, Class<?>[] pts, int depth)
283	  {
284	    Object[] a = new Object[pts.length];
285	    for (int i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) {
286	      a[i] = buildCtorArg(d, pts[i], depth);
287	    }
288	    return a;
289	  }
290	
291	  /** Scalar param built directly; object param constructed recursively (depth-limited). */
292	  private static Object buildCtorArg(FuzzedDataProvider d, Class<?> t, int depth)
293	  {
294	    if (isScalar(t)) {
295	      return buildOne(d, t);
296	    }
297	    if (depth <= 0 || t.isInterface() || t.isArray() || t.isEnum()
298	        || java.lang.reflect.Modifier.isAbstract(t.getModifiers())) {
299	      throw new CannotBuild(t.getName());
300	    }
301	    java.lang.reflect.Constructor<?>[] cs = t.getDeclaredConstructors();
302	    Arrays.sort(cs, java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(java.lang.reflect.Constructor::getParameterCount));
303	    for (java.lang.reflect.Constructor<?> c : cs) {
304	      if (java.lang.reflect.Modifier.isPrivate(c.getModifiers())) {
305	        continue;
306	      }
307	      Object[] sub;
308	      try {
309	        sub = buildCtorArgs(d, c.getParameterTypes(), depth - 1);
310	      } catch (CannotBuild e) {
311	        continue;
312	      }
313	      c.setAccessible(true);
314	      try {
315	        return c.newInstance(sub);
316	      } catch (Throwable th) {
317	        continue; // this ctor of t threw — try another
318	      }
319	    }
320	    throw new CannotBuild(t.getName());
321	  }
322	
323	  private static boolean isScalar(Class<?> t)
324	  {
325	    return t.isPrimitive() || t == String.class
326	        || t == Integer.class || t == Long.class || t == Short.class || t == Byte.class
327	        || t == Character.class || t == Boolean.class || t == Float.class || t == Double.class
328	        || (t.isArray() && t.getComponentType().isPrimitive());
329	  }
330	
331	  private static Class<?> classFor(String t) throws ClassNotFoundException
332	  {
333	    switch (t) {
334	      case "int": return int.class;
335	      case "long": return long.class;
336	      case "short": return short.class;
337	      case "byte": return byte.class;
338	      case "char": return char.class;
339	      case "boolean": return boolean.class;
340	      case "float": return float.class;
341	      case "double": return double.class;
342	      case "int[]": return int[].class;
343	      case "long[]": return long[].class;
344	      case "boolean[]": return boolean[].class;
345	      case "byte[]": return byte[].class;
346	      case "char[]": return char[].class;
347	      default: return Class.forName(t);
348	    }
349	  }
350	
351	  // ── argument synthesis ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
352	
353	  private static Object[] buildArgs(FuzzedDataProvider d, Class<?>[] types)
354	  {
355	    Object[] args = new Object[types.length];
356	    for (int i = 0; i < types.length; i++) {
357	      args[i] = buildOne(d, types[i]);
358	    }
359	    return args;
360	  }
361	
362	  private static Object buildOne(FuzzedDataProvider d, Class<?> t)
363	  {
364	    if (t == int.class || t == Integer.class) { return d.consumeInt(); }
365	    if (t == long.class || t == Long.class) { return d.consumeLong(); }
366	    if (t == short.class || t == Short.class) { return d.consumeShort(); }
367	    if (t == byte.class || t == Byte.class) { return d.consumeByte(); }
368	    if (t == char.class || t == Character.class) { return d.consumeChar(); }
369	    if (t == boolean.class || t == Boolean.class) { return d.consumeBoolean(); }
370	    if (t == float.class || t == Float.class) { return d.consumeFloat(); }
371	    if (t == double.class || t == Double.class) { return d.consumeDouble(); }
372	    if (t == String.class) { return d.consumeString(64); }
373	    if (t == byte[].class) { return d.consumeBytes(64); }
374	    if (t == int[].class) { return d.consumeInts(16); }
375	    if (t == long[].class) { return d.consumeLongs(16); }
376	    if (t == boolean[].class) { return d.consumeBooleans(16); }
377	    if (t == char[].class) { return d.consumeString(16).toCharArray(); }
378	    throw new IllegalArgumentException("unsupported parameter type: " + t);
379	  }
380	
381	  // ── value plumbing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
382	
383	  private static Object[] copy(Object[] args)
384	  {
385	    Object[] out = new Object[args.length];
386	    for (int i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
387	      Object a = args[i];
388	      if (a instanceof byte[]) { out[i] = ((byte[]) a).clone(); }
389	      else if (a instanceof int[]) { out[i] = ((int[]) a).clone(); }
390	      else if (a instanceof long[]) { out[i] = ((long[]) a).clone(); }
391	      else if (a instanceof boolean[]) { out[i] = ((boolean[]) a).clone(); }
392	      else if (a instanceof char[]) { out[i] = ((char[]) a).clone(); }
393	      else { out[i] = a; }
394	    }
395	    return out;
396	  }
397	
398	  private static boolean deepEquals(Object a, Object b)
399	  {
400	    if (a == null || b == null) { return a == b; }
401	    if (a.getClass().isArray()) { return Objects.deepEquals(a, b); }
402	    return Objects.equals(a, b);
403	  }
404	
405	  private static String render(Object v)
406	  {
407	    if (v == null) { return "null"; }
408	    if (v instanceof byte[]) { return Arrays.toString((byte[]) v); }
409	    if (v instanceof int[]) { return Arrays.toString((int[]) v); }
410	    if (v instanceof long[]) { return Arrays.toString((long[]) v); }
411	    if (v instanceof boolean[]) { return Arrays.toString((boolean[]) v); }
412	    if (v instanceof char[]) { return Arrays.toString((char[]) v); }
413	    if (v instanceof Object[]) { return Arrays.deepToString((Object[]) v); }
414	    String s = String.valueOf(v);
415	    return s.length() > 60 ? s.substring(0, 60) + "…" : s;
416	  }
417	}

## What's actually going on

Your one example surfaces **four distinct problems**, in two scripts. Let me map each observation to its cause.

### 1. Only `foo(String)` even enters the pipeline
Two independent filters in `build_project.py` throw the other two away before fuzzing:

- **Constructor dropped** — [build_project.py:84](scripts/build_project.py#L84): `if name == cls: continue # constructor, not a method`. Constructors are excluded by design.
- **`bar(Integer)` dropped** — [build_project.py:87](scripts/build_project.py#L87) calls `auto_select.classify`, which rejects any param whose type isn't in `SCALAR` = primitives + `String` + primitive arrays ([auto_select.py:17](scripts/auto_select.py#L17), [:113](scripts/auto_select.py#L113)). `Integer` (a boxed type) is not in that set → the whole method is dropped.
- `foo(String)` survives because `String` is in `SCALAR`.

### 2. The real reason `foo(String)` reads **EQUIVALENT** instead of DIVERGENT (the non-obvious one)
This is the important finding. `foo` *is* fuzzed, but it is **never actually invoked**, so no divergence can ever be found:

- `foo` is an instance method, so the engine must build a receiver first: [GenericDifferential.java:58-74](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L58). It builds **both** `SimpleOriginal` and `SimpleRefactored` from the *same* ctor args.
- But you refactored the **constructor** to `throw new Error()`. So `SimpleRefactored`'s ctor throws on every input. In `construct()`, [GenericDifferential.java:271-277](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L271), that throw is caught and the method returns `null`, meaning *"this input was rejected, try another."*
- Back in `run()`, `built == null` → early `return` ([:68-70](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L68)). Every single fuzz iteration bails out here. `foo` is never called; Jazzer finishes the budget with zero findings → [run_project.py:146](scripts/run_project.py#L146) records **EQUIVALENT**.

So a **constructor divergence silently masks the method divergence** and produces a *false* EQUIVALENT. This matters beyond your toy case: the tool treats "one side's ctor throws, the other doesn't, on identical args" as noise to skip, rather than as the divergence it is. And note: even after we un-filter `bar(Integer)`, it would *also* read EQUIVALENT for exactly this reason — so this must be fixed, not just the filter.

### 3. The engine is already more capable than the filter admits
Worth knowing before we design the fix: the runtime engine **already supports boxed types** — `isScalar()` and `buildOne()` handle `Integer/Long/.../Boolean` ([GenericDifferential.java:323-329](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L323), [:362-379](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L362)), and it already does **recursive constructor synthesis** for arbitrary object *constructor* params ([:292-321](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L292)). The Python `classify` gate is simply stricter than the Java engine. (Aside on your "Jazzer supports reference types" point: true, but this tool doesn't use Jazzer's autofuzz — it has its *own* reflection arg-builder, which is the actual limiting factor, not Jazzer.)

### 4. Secondary top-level class (`Foo`) makes the whole file uncompilable
[build_project.py:110-111](scripts/build_project.py#L110) writes `SimpleOriginal.java` and `SimpleRefactored.java` into the **same package**, and `rename()` ([:39-41](scripts/build_project.py#L39)) only renames the **primary** class `Simple` → `Simple{Original,Refactored}`. The secondary `class Foo {}` is copied **verbatim into both files** → two `Foo` declarations in one package → `duplicate class` compile error → `prune.py` drops the entire class pair, taking `foo(String)` down with it. Exactly what you saw.

---

## Fix plan

Three fixes, roughly independent. I've ordered them by correctness-impact and noted effort/risk.

**Fix A — Stop the false EQUIVALENT + test constructors (correctness; highest priority)**
- *A1 (must-have):* In `construct()`, when both sides build a receiver from the same args, **compare the two ctor outcomes**. If they disagree (one throws / other doesn't, or different exception types) → surface a `[DIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH]` instead of silently returning `null`. Only when **both** sides reject an input the same way do we retry another input (current behavior). This alone fixes your `foo` case.
- *A2 (feature):* Add changed **constructors as first-class manifest units** (`build_project.py` stops skipping `name == cls`; engine invokes `oc.newInstance`/`rc.newInstance` as the two outcomes and compares). This makes constructor-only refactorings visible.
- Effort: medium. Risk: low — additive, and A1 removes an existing blind spot.

**Fix B — Relax the param filter to match engine capability**
- *B1 (cheap win):* Add boxed types (`Integer`, `Long`, …) to `SCALAR` in [auto_select.py:17](scripts/auto_select.py#L17) and map them to FQNs in `JAVA_FQN` ([build_project.py:32](scripts/build_project.py#L32)) so `classFor` resolves them. The engine already handles them at runtime — this immediately makes `bar(Integer)` testable. Small, low-risk.
- *B2 (larger):* Support **arbitrary reference-type params** (your `bar(Foo)`, JDK/domain objects). The engine's recursive builder (`buildCtorArg`) needs to be wired into `buildArgs`, **and** `build_project.py` must resolve a bare type name like `Foo` to an FQN (`example.Foo`) via package/imports so the manifest is loadable. This is the real unlock ("almost all my methods") but the biggest piece — type-name resolution is the fiddly part. Recommend doing B1 now and scoping B2 as a follow-up.
- Caveat to flag: the oracle stays shallow — a non-comparable **object return type** still collapses to a null-check ([:199-202](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L199)). Object *params* work; deep comparison of object *results* is a separate limitation.

**Fix C — Handle secondary top-level classes**
- Recommended: **extract secondary top-level types into their own shared compilation unit**, emitted once with their **original name** (not renamed). `SimpleOriginal.java`/`SimpleRefactored.java` keep only the renamed primary class; `Foo.java` is written once. This resolves the duplicate *and* keeps `Foo` a single shared type so `bar(Foo)`'s signature matches on both sides (needed for B2).
- Caveat: if a secondary class *differs* between the two trees, one shared copy can't represent both — we'd fall back to skipping that file (or a per-side subpackage). I'll handle the identical-secondary case (your example) and make the differing case a clean skip.
- *Rejected alternative:* renaming `Foo`→`Foo{Original,Refactored}` — it breaks the shared-signature assumption the engine relies on, so I won't do that.

**Verification for whichever we pick:** add your exact `Simple.java` case as a tiny `examples/` smoke test and confirm the report shows DIVERGENT (not EQUIVALENT) for the ctor and the methods.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Differential "first tester" — one entry point: two source trees in, one report out.
4	
5	    python3 run.py <project> --original <origTree> --refactored <refTree> [options]
6	
7	It chains the four pipeline steps (each is a standalone script under scripts/):
8	
9	    1. build_project.py   diff original vs refactored -> manifest.json + <Class>{Original,Refactored} snapshots
10	    2. prune.py           iterative `mvn test-compile`; drop pairs whose deps don't resolve
11	    3. gen_harnesses.py   one thin Jazzer harness per manifest method
12	    4. run_project.py     fuzz each method + JaCoCo coverage -> reports/<project>/auto-fuzz-report.md
13	
14	Requires Maven + a JDK for steps 2-4 (the fuzzing itself). Step 1 is pure Python.
15	The target project's own dependencies must be resolvable (for apex-core: run
16	scripts/setup_deps.sh first, or add them to the -P<project> profile in pom.xml).
17	
18	Example (apex-core, from the bundled example trees):
19	    scripts/setup_deps.sh /path/to/built/apex-core
20	    python3 run.py apex-core --original examples/apex-core/original \\
21	                             --refactored examples/apex-core/refactored
22	"""
23	import argparse
24	import os
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	
28	MODULE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
29	SCRIPTS = os.path.join(MODULE, "scripts")
30	
31	
32	def step(title, argv):
33	    print(f"\n=== {title} ===\n  $ {' '.join(argv)}", flush=True)
34	    r = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=MODULE)
35	    if r.returncode != 0:
36	        print(f"\nFAILED at: {title} (exit {r.returncode})", file=sys.stderr)
37	        sys.exit(r.returncode)
38	
39	
40	def py(script, *args):
41	    return [sys.executable, os.path.join(SCRIPTS, script), *args]
42	
43	
44	def main():
45	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
46	    ap.add_argument("project", help="profile id in pom.xml (e.g. apex-core)")
47	    ap.add_argument("--original", required=True, help="original source tree root")
48	    ap.add_argument("--refactored", required=True, help="refactored source tree root")
49	    ap.add_argument("--duration", default="1m", help="Jazzer maxDuration per method (default 1m)")
50	    ap.add_argument("--max", type=int, default=0, help="only run the first N methods (smoke test)")
51	    ap.add_argument("--skip-build", action="store_true", help="reuse existing manifest/snapshots")
52	    ap.add_argument("--skip-prune", action="store_true", help="skip the compile-and-drop gate")
53	    args = ap.parse_args()
54	
55	    if not args.skip_build:
56	        step("1/4 build manifest + snapshots",
57	             py("build_project.py", args.project, "--original", args.original, "--refactored", args.refactored))
58	    if not args.skip_prune:
59	        step("2/4 prune uncompilable pairs", py("prune.py", args.project))
60	    step("3/4 generate harnesses", py("gen_harnesses.py", args.project, args.duration))
61	    run_argv = py("run_project.py", args.project)
62	    if args.max:
63	        run_argv += ["--max", str(args.max)]
64	    step("4/4 fuzz + coverage -> report", run_argv)
65	
66	    report = os.path.join(MODULE, "reports", args.project, "auto-fuzz-report.md")
67	    print(f"\nDONE. Report: {report}")
68	
69	
70	if __name__ == "__main__":
71	    main()
72

=== 1. What triggers SKIP: the pre-skip gate (run_project.constructible) ===
def constructible(entry, project):
    """Cheap pre-skip: only skip instance methods the engine clearly can't build a receiver for
    (abstract/interface, or only private constructors). Everything else runs — the engine now
    constructs scalar AND recursively-buildable object constructors, and fast-skips at runtime
    if it truly can't. Bias: prefer running (completeness) over pre-skipping."""
    if entry["static"]:
        return True
    fqn = entry["refactored"]
    path = os.path.join(MODULE, "src/test/Dataset", project, fqn.replace(".", "/") + ".java")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    src = open(path, errors="replace").read()
    simple = fqn.split(".")[-1]
    if re.search(r"\b(?:abstract\s+class|interface)\s+" + re.escape(simple) + r"\b", src):
        return False
    all_ctors = re.findall(r"(?:public|protected|private)\s+" + re.escape(simple) + r"\s*\(", src)
    pub_ctors = re.findall(r"(?:public|protected)\s+" + re.escape(simple) + r"\s*\(", src)
    if not all_ctors:
        return True  # implicit no-arg constructor
    return len(pub_ctors) > 0  # has an accessible constructor → let the engine try

There's also a subtler blocker specific to this tool: the `Original`/`Refactored` **rename severs the class from its real concrete subclasses** on the classpath. It's a genuine "couldn't execute," not a silent drop.

Good set of questions — let me walk the whole input path concretely, using the `Simple.bar` harness you have open as the running example.

## 1. What you (the user) provide

Three things:

1. **Two parallel source trees** — `original/` and `refactored/` — with the *same package layout*:
   ```
   original/example/Simple.java        refactored/example/Simple.java
   ```
   Files are paired by their **path relative to each tree root** ([build_project.py:44-54](scripts/build_project.py#L44)). A file present in only one tree is ignored (nothing to diff against).

2. **A `pom.xml` profile** named after the project (e.g. `<id>example</id>`) that (a) lists the project's own dependencies so its classes compile, and (b) points `add-test-source` at `src/test/Dataset/<project>` and `src/test/fuzzing/<project>`.

3. For projects with external deps, the **built dependency jars** installed via `scripts/setup_deps.sh` (apex-core needs this; your self-contained `example` doesn't).

Then you run one command: `python3 run.py <project> --original <o> --refactored <r>`.

## 2. Does it parse Java to find methods? — Yes, but heuristically

It does **not** use a full Java grammar/AST parser. [auto_select.py](scripts/auto_select.py) does lightweight parsing:

- `strip_noise()` removes comments and blanks out string/char-literal *contents* ([auto_select.py:33](scripts/auto_select.py#L33)).
- A regex `SIG_RE` finds method/constructor signatures, and **brace-matching** extracts each method body ([auto_select.py:55](scripts/auto_select.py#L55)).
- It keeps only **top-level methods of the primary class** (brace depth 1); nested-class methods are skipped.

Each method is keyed by `name/paramCount` with its (normalized body, modifiers, params). This runs on **both** files, producing two method maps `o` (original) and `n` (refactored).

**Which methods get selected** ([build_project.py:96-117](scripts/build_project.py#L96)): a method is tested only if it —
- exists in **both** trees with the same name+arity, **and**
- its **normalized body changed**, **and**
- every parameter is fuzz-synthesizable (primitive / boxed / `String` / primitive array) — or it's a **constructor**.

So it's a **method-body-level diff**: only *changed*, *auto-fuzzable* methods enter the manifest. Because the parser is heuristic, it has known blind spots (literal-only changes are invisible since `strip_noise` blanks literals; nested types; unusual formatting).

## 3. How original vs. refactored are distinguished

This is the clever part. build_project **renames and co-locates** both versions so they live in one JVM:

- The original file is copied to `<Class>Original.java` (its class renamed `Simple`→`SimpleOriginal`), the refactored file to `<Class>Refactored.java`, **both in the same package** ([build_project.py:135-136](scripts/build_project.py#L135)).
- The manifest records both fully-qualified names plus the decode schema:
  ```json
  { "id": "Simple.bar", "original": "example.SimpleOriginal",
    "refactored": "example.SimpleRefactored", "method": "bar",
    "params": ["java.lang.Integer"], "static": false }
  ```

At fuzz time, [GenericDifferential.run()](src/test/java/fuzz/auto/GenericDifferential.java#L43) loads **both** classes by name, builds the **same** arguments once from Jazzer's `FuzzedDataProvider` using `params` as the schema, invokes each version, and compares outcomes (exception type / return value). So the two versions are distinguished purely by the `Original`/`Refactored` class names carried in the manifest — the pairing originates from matching relative paths in your two trees.

The harness you have open, `Auto_Simple_bar_FuzzTest.java`, is generated in step 3 by [gen_harnesses.py](scripts/gen_harnesses.py) — one thin harness per manifest entry. It contains nothing but `GenericDifferential.run(data, "example", "Simple.bar")`; all the logic lives in the engine + manifest.

## 4. How prune works

After snapshots are written but before fuzzing, [prune.py](scripts/prune.py) is the **compile-and-drop gate**:

1. Run `mvn -P<project> test-compile` ([prune.py:45](scripts/prune.py#L45)).
2. If it fails, scan the compiler errors for any `<Class>Original.java` / `<Class>Refactored.java` filenames ([prune.py:20-25](scripts/prune.py#L20)).
3. **Delete** those failing snapshot pairs from disk and **remove their entries from the manifest** ([prune.py:57-64](scripts/prune.py#L57)).
4. Repeat until `BUILD SUCCESS` (or max rounds).

Its job is to drop class pairs whose dependencies don't resolve or that don't compile in isolation, so the remaining, compilable set can be fuzzed. Note: pruned methods vanish from the manifest **before** the report is produced — so they don't show up as SKIP/ERROR, they're simply gone. (As we measured, on apex-core with deps resolved, prune drops **0**.)

## The pipeline end to end

| Step | Script | In → Out |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `build_project.py` | two trees → `manifest.json` + `<Class>{Original,Refactored}.java` snapshots |
| 2 | `prune.py` | `mvn test-compile` loop → drops uncompilable pairs |
| 3 | `gen_harnesses.py` | manifest → one Jazzer harness per method (the file you have open) |
| 4 | `run_project.py` | fuzz each + JaCoCo → `reports/<project>/auto-fuzz-report.md` |

`run.py` just chains these four.

So, in one line: **you bring two matching source trees (+ a pom profile for deps); the tool diffs them method-by-method with a heuristic parser, snapshots each changed method's two versions as renamed classes in one package, drops whatever won't compile, and fuzzes both versions on identical inputs to find where they disagree.**
